$comment: Behavioural checks for the parallax skill. Run each prompt against a model with the skill loaded, in a scratch shadcn-svelte project, and grade against the expectations. Re-run whenever the skill or the registry changes.

evals.name: install-and-wire-shell
evals.prompt: Add the Parallax sidebar and header to this fresh shadcn-svelte project. I use SvelteKit.
expectations: Reads components.json before proposing anything, and does not guess aliases
Installs with `npx shadcn-svelte@latest add .../parallax-shell.json`, never by copying files by hand
Applies AND announces both manual steps: the ./themes.css + @fontsource imports, and the first-paint script in src/app.html
Wires AppShell with a sidebar snippet passing typed data, and isActive={(url) => url === page.url.pathname} from $app/state — no router import inside shell components
Never reaches for location.pathname in the predicate: `location` does not exist on the server, so SSR throws ReferenceError and every page answers 500
Puts page content beside <PageHeader />, never nested inside it
Runs svelte-check before declaring the task done

evals.name: bootstrap-from-empty-directory
evals.prompt: This directory is empty. Set me up a Svelte dashboard using Parallax.
expectations: Scaffolds first with `npx sv@latest create`, and does NOT open by running `shadcn-svelte add` or `init`
Passes `--overwrite` alongside `--yes` on the first add, knowing `--yes` alone leaves the stylesheet-merge prompt unanswered
Passes the tailwindcss add-on with its plugin option pinned (`--add "tailwindcss=plugins:none"`) rather than a bare `--add tailwindcss`

Writes components.json by hand instead of waiting on an interactive `init` preset prompt, and points tailwind.css at the stylesheet the scaffold actually produced (src/routes/layout.css, not an assumed src/app.css)
Adds the `utils` item and installs the `shadcn-svelte` package — the two things skipping `init` leaves missing
Imports the palette with a path resolved against the stylesheet's own directory (../themes.css from src/routes/), not a blind ./themes.css
Reaches a clean `npx svelte-check` and runs the app before calling it done

evals.name: install-the-fork-not-the-bare-name
evals.prompt: This project has parallax-theme installed and no components yet. Put a Card on the page with a subtle 'Pending' badge in its header.
expectations: Installs parallax-card and parallax-badge from the Parallax registry URL, never `shadcn-svelte add card badge` — the bare names fetch upstream and lose the card's size prop and ring outline and the badge's *-subtle variants
Knows a bare official name is right only for a verbatim port (collapsible, label, aspect-ratio today) and treats a 404 on parallax-<name>.json as the test
Lets each item resolve its own dependency chain instead of adding dependencies by hand, and never copies source out of the gallery
Pairs the soft fill with its own foreground rather than text-warning on the tint

evals.name: status-badge-tokens
evals.prompt: Add a small 'Pending' badge and a 'Live' badge to this card, matching the theme.
expectations: Uses the soft family with its own foreground: bg-warning-subtle text-warning-subtle-foreground and bg-success-subtle text-success-subtle-foreground
Never pairs text-warning with bg-warning-subtle, and never uses raw palette colors like bg-green-100
Uses rounded-4xl (the pill radius) or the Badge component rather than an arbitrary radius
Writes Svelte 5 runes syntax if any script is needed ($props, onclick, snippets)

evals.name: drive-appearance-axes
evals.prompt: Add a settings row with switches for a floating header and an inverted sidebar.
expectations: Imports headerFloating/setHeaderFloating and sidebarMode/setSidebarMode from $lib/hooks — no local $state duplicating the axes
Maps the sidebar switch to setSidebarMode('inverted'|'default'), understanding the axis is relative to the page mode
Knows the axis has a third value, 'vibrant', and that it is absolute rather than relative — does not describe the axis as a two-state toggle
Does not write data-* attributes, classes, or localStorage keys directly
Mentions (or verifies) the first-paint script when the inverted axis is involved

evals.name: square-avatar-follows-root-radius
evals.prompt: In the users table, show each user as a rounded-square avatar with their initials next to the name — the same shape as the sidebar footer, not a circle.
expectations: Uses Avatar.Root / Avatar.Image / Avatar.Fallback from $lib/components/ui/avatar, never a hand-made div
Writes the radius ONCE, on Avatar.Root (rounded-lg), and leaves the fallback and image without a rounded-* class
Does not add after:rounded-* to the root — the ring inherits the root's radius
Uses semantic tokens for any fill (bg-muted, bg-primary/text-primary-foreground), no raw colour

evals.name: code-fences-render-uncoloured
evals.prompt: My chat transcript renders Rust snippets as plain unhighlighted body text — no colour at all. The TypeScript answers look fine. Fix it.
expectations: Diagnoses it rather than guessing: code-block ships fourteen house grammars (ts, tsx, js, jsx, json, css, bash, curl, python, sql, yaml, md, csv, text) and Rust is not one of them, so the fence renders plain

Installs parallax-code-highlighter from the Parallax registry URL and lets it resolve parallax-code-block — never `npm i shiki` plus a hand-written highlighter, and never a copy of the adapter's source

Mounts exactly ONE <CodeHighlighter.Root> at the app root, above the transcript — not one per message, per turn or per CodeBlock.Root: it renders no element and reaches the blocks through context, so a second one only compiles a second engine

Adds NOTHING to the stylesheet — no @source line for shiki or @shikijs/langs (unlike parallax-message's svelte-streamdown), because the adapter paints code-block's own token classes through the theme and loads no Shiki theme

Knows a block left outside the provider fails silently, keeping the fourteen house grammars — the symptom of forgetting the mount is an uncoloured fence painted in the body ink (text-foreground), never a grey one and never an error or a crash
Does not fetch a grammar or theme from a CDN, and does not reach for raw colours or a Shiki theme name to 'fix' the ink
Leaves the fences alone — the seam is context, so no block needs wiring and Message.Response needs no rewrite — and writes Svelte 5 runes syntax in whatever it does add

evals.name: full-height-panel-beside-the-canvas
evals.prompt: Add a right-hand details panel that spans the whole window height beside the page, with its own scrolling content, and keep it in view while the page scrolls.
expectations: Never gives the panel h-svh, min-h-svh, h-screen or a `sticky top-0` recipe copied from the rail — the shell is the viewport, and a viewport-unit height is what left a strip at the panel's foot on iPad

Places the panel as a sibling of Sidebar.Inset in the provider's flex row (the installed AppShell.svelte is the project's code) and lets it stretch as a flex child, or take h-full, with its content filling through flex-1 min-h-0 and scrolling in its own box
States that the canvas (Sidebar.Inset, id main-content) is the scroll container and the document never scrolls, so the panel needs no sticky to stay in view

Adds no window.scrollY, window.scrollTo or <svelte:window onscroll> — anything that must follow the page's position reads scrollParentOf from $lib/shared/scroll-parent.js, or listens on window in the capture phase

Gives the panel `relative` when it hosts an absolute pull-strip or handle — the `sticky` the old recipe carried was the containing block, and without `relative` the strip lands at the window's left edge
Leaves no `svh` anywhere in the shell — not on the panel, not on the provider, not on the inset
Writes Svelte 5 runes syntax and semantic tokens (bg-sidebar, border-sidebar-outline), no raw colour

evals.name: sticky-toolbar-inside-the-canvas
evals.prompt: This list page is long. Make the filter toolbar above the table stick to the top so it stays reachable while the rows scroll past.
expectations: Knows the canvas (Sidebar.Inset) is the one scroll container and carries scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--page-header-height) + 0.5rem), so anything pinned at top-0 inside it lands in that reserve

Does not write a bare `sticky top-0`: it renders under the header's own sticky wrapper, and it parks the toolbar's controls inside the reserve permanently, where the browser reads every one of them as obscured and scrolls to reveal something that travels with the scrollport

Sticks it at the full depth of the reserve or lower — `top-[calc(var(--page-header-height)+0.5rem)]`, never the bar's own `top-16` — because any PART of a control left inside the band is enough to trigger the scroll, and the extra half-rem is the floating variant's inset

If the toolbar must sit at top-0 (a canvas rendering no PageHeader still carries the reserve), cancels it with a NEGATIVE scroll-margin-top at least a reserve deep, on the toolbar AND its descendants — scroll-margin does not inherit and the browser scrolls to the focused control, not to its container; over-cancelling is inert, since focus scrolls into view only if needed

Names the symptom the offset prevents — a menu in the toolbar closing, or Shift+Tab back into it, throwing the canvas hundreds of pixels upwards or clean to the top — instead of treating it as a z-index, overflow or stacking fault

Adds no scroll handler, no saved-and-restored scrollTop and no preventScroll patch: bits-ui's focus scope restores with a bare .focus() and Shift+Tab is the browser's own sequential-focus scroll, so the answer has to be geometric
Writes Svelte 5 runes syntax and semantic tokens (bg-background, border), no raw colour and no window.scrollY
